heroCommands.comment: Set up Context7 for your coding agent

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Context7 gives AI coding agents up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples for the libraries you use. It works as an MCP server or as a CLI plus skill, so agents like Claude Code and Cursor fetch current docs instead of relying on old training data.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents often produce outdated examples or invent APIs that don't exist because their training data is old. Context7 pulls documentation from the source into the agent's context when you ask about a library.
whoFor: Claude Code, Cursor and OpenCode users
Library authors who want their docs available to agents
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it to cut outdated and invented API suggestions from your coding agent with one setup command. A free API key is recommended for higher rate limits; the backend service is not open source.
requirements: A coding agent or MCP client
Recommended: a free Context7 API key

overview: After setup, you add 'use context7' to a prompt, such as asking for a Next.js proxy that checks a JWT, and the agent fetches current docs and examples for that library. You can name a library ID like /supabase/supabase to skip matching, or mention a version to get version-specific docs.

It works in two modes: CLI plus skills, where a skill guides the agent to run ctx7 commands, or MCP, where the agent calls resolve-library-id and query-docs tools. npx ctx7 setup authenticates with OAuth, creates an API key and installs the right setup for Cursor, Claude Code or OpenCode.

This repository holds the MCP server source; the API backend, parsing and crawling engines are private. Library docs are community-contributed, and Upstash says it cannot guarantee their accuracy, completeness or security.
